context.reviewedBy: Codex; evidence-backed backfill, pending owner review

who.summary: Alia is the accountable owner and authorial voice. The intended readers are adults seeking practical understanding of their teeth and dental care. Agents assist research and drafting under the editorial contract; the material is education, not an individual treating dentist.

what.summary: The Adult Teeth Guide: How to Keep Your Teeth Healthy for Life. A consumer book, source ledger, chapter manuscripts, review reports and routine cheat sheets, with a generated/assembled reading manuscript and versioned release artifacts.

when.summary: The earliest root commit in the inspected, reachable history is dated 2026-07-15T23:15:55-07:00. This bounds retained source history; it does not establish the original idea or business founding date. The inspected README records source version 0.1.3. Editorial status and outstanding claims belong in reviews/; neither a Git release nor an assembled manuscript establishes commercial publication.

where.summary: Source and editorial work live in aliawilkinson/adult-dental-care-book on GitHub. Canonical portfolio identity is product:adult-dental-care-book in MetadataDB. Distribution outside GitHub and a commercial publisher have not been established by this backfill.

why.summary: Alia wanted a practical reference she could return to, plus a bathroom-mirror routine cheat sheet, and saw value for other adults. The book aims to explain mechanisms and tradeoffs so readers can participate knowledgeably in their care.

how.summary: Treat the manuscript as versioned source: preserve the approved outline and voice, edit one chapter at a time, track claims and international evidence, keep unresolved author decisions visible, and assemble/review the reading manuscript before release.

setup.summary: Clone the repository and read AGENTS.md, outline.md, author-voice.md, editorial-rules.md, claims-policy.md and international-research-standard.md before drafting. The source is Markdown; no production runtime or database is required to begin editorial work.

verify.summary: Review each changed chapter against the outline, claim/source policy and international research standard; record unresolved claims and author decisions in reviews/. Check the assembled book against chapter sources. scripts/README.md is only a placeholder, so no executable assembly/test suite is claimed.

deploy.summary: Use feature branches and reviewed PRs. The release workflow calls shared SemVer/Release Please workflows; an approved release PR creates a tag and packages the manuscript/source with checksums and provenance. Commercial publication, publisher access and retailer distribution are not specified.

operate.summary: Maintain source citations, claim currency, editorial progress, author decisions, VERSION and CHANGELOG through reviewed work. Recheck clinical claims when revising rather than treating an old source release as current medical evidence.

recover.summary: Git source and release artifacts are recovery starting points, but no independently retained backup, rights/access succession procedure, complete assembly command or tested restore is documented. Alia must record and verify these before relying on long-term recovery.
